history.summary: New TOP 2026 leasehold near Bartley/Serangoon, 2BR at $1.64M / $2,240psf. Strong arena record (372-47, MMR 1532, score 694) and resale-only URA of 6.5%/yr are attractive, but the project is small (115 units), the 4.07% bias-adjusted rate reflects new-launch inflation, and the smallest 2BR stacks face landed/road with west-sun exposure.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $2,240psf sits just under the $2,346 URA median, so it is not overpriced for a brand-new unit, and Wee Hur has a solid build reputation. But at 115 units liquidity is thin, the headline 6.5% resale CAGR is inflated by new-launch base effect (system-adjusted rate is 4.07%, in line with OCR), and the cheap 2BR stacks carry road noise / west sun. Decent but not a standout entry at this price.
red_flags: Small 115-unit development — thinner resale liquidity and limited amenities
New-launch pricing: 6.5% resale CAGR likely inflated, adjusted rate only ~4.1%
Cheapest 2BR stacks face landed/road with west-sun exposure
Sub-1:1 carpark ratio and high maintenance noted in forums
catalysts: Brand-new 2026 completion — no immediate capex, full lease
Walkable to CC12 Bartley MRT (630m), near popular schools
Asking PSF below district URA median leaves modest headroom

history.summary: A brand-new (2026 TOP) compact 1,044 sqft 3BR from boutique 115-unit Bartley Vue at a steep $2,395 psf and $2.5M quantum. The system already flagged new-launch bias and discounted the headline rate to 4.07%/yr; at this price/PSF on a tiny development with a high quantum, the risk/reward is poor.
history.rating_rationale: Three things stack against this as an investment: (1) $2,395 psf is above the $2,346 district median and you are buying at peak new-launch pricing — the bias-adjusted appreciation is only 4.07%/yr (vs 6.47% resale-only), so the system is explicitly warning the headline CAGR re-introduces developer inflation; (2) $2.5M for a compact 1,044 sqft 3BR pushes past the deep-buyer sweet spot into a thinner pool, with little built-in upside; (3) only 115 units = boutique, illiquid, minimal facilities, and the MRT is a 630m/8-min walk with Circle-Line-only access. Buying a just-TOP unit at developer-peak PSF in D19 with no discount and a high quantum is the classic overpay-at-launch trap. Avoid for a 5-7yr investment hold.

catalysts: Brand-new 2026 build (no defect/maintenance legacy) near Bartley MRT in central D19
Small exclusive development appeals to a niche own-stay buyer at resale
Wee Hur build with smart-home/modern spec
